original_question: Let X be a complete length CAT(0) space, not assumed locally compact, and let K be a compact subset of X. Is the closed convex hull of K, meaning the intersection of all closed convex subsets of X that contain K, necessarily compact?
target_in_paper: Section 12, open problem "Convex hull in CAT(0)": the paper asks whether the closed convex hull of a compact subset of a complete CAT(0) length space must be compact. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual question. It has the correct ambient setting (a complete CAT(0) length space), the correct hypothesis on the subset (compactness), the correct object (the closed convex hull), the correct meaning of that hull as an intersection of closed convex supersets, and it correctly keeps local compactness out of the assumptions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
missing_details: To match the paper's setup literally, one can make the notion of convexity explicit: in a geodesic metric space, a subset C is convex if for any two points x,y in C, every geodesic from x to y lies in C. In a CAT(0) space this is mostly an explicitness issue, since geodesics are unique. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
refined_question: Let X be a complete CAT(0) length space, and let K be a compact subset of X. A subset C of X is called convex if every geodesic joining two points of C is contained in C. Is the closed convex hull of K—that is, the intersection of all closed convex subsets of X that contain K—necessarily compact, even without assuming that X is locally compact? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
justification: This is the exact Section 12 problem rather than a broader neighboring question. The paper first defines convex subsets and the closed convex hull in a geodesic metric space, then asks whether a compact subset K of a complete CAT(0) length space has compact closed convex hull, and immediately notes that local compactness is not assumed and that the locally compact case is evident. Your draft already tracks that formulation closely; the only real paper-faithful refinement is to spell out the geodesic meaning of convexity so the question is fully stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
